_read_me: Every number the planner uses that is not typed in by the family lives here. Each entry has value, unit, source and as_of. A value of null with source TODO means it has not been checked yet; the app shows 'not set yet' instead of guessing. Values were looked up with help from an AI assistant from the sources listed; NEEDS_OWNER.md lists what Sahas still needs to confirm. After editing, run python tools/build.py so the site picks up the change.

default_interest_rate.source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey: 'The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 7.32% as of October 22, 2026': https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms
default_interest_rate.note: National weekly average. A family's real rate depends on credit, points and lender, so they can type their own. Update weekly or before the video.

default_term_years.source: Matches the loan the rate above is for (Freddie Mac surveys the 30-year fixed)

minimum_down_payment_percent.source: My Home by Freddie Mac, 'Unlock Homeownership with Just 3% Down': Home Possible 'provides down payment options as low as 3%': https://myhome.freddiemac.com/buying/3-percent-down-payment
minimum_down_payment_percent.note: The lowest down payment the planner allows. Many loans need more; some programs (FHA, VA) differ.

estimate_to_sale_price_ratio.unit: model estimate divided by sale price (median)
estimate_to_sale_price_ratio.source: This project's sales check (housing_model_v2.ipynb, saved in data/summary.json under alpharetta_sales_check, 2025): 308 Alpharetta homes sold in 2025, and the model's estimate was a median 0.78 of the sale price (county values were 0.786).
estimate_to_sale_price_ratio.note: Measured in Alpharetta (Fulton County), not Forsyth: Forsyth has no open sale records yet. The planner divides each estimate by this to get a likely sale price (about 28% higher), so homes are not judged as cheaper than they sell for. Replace with a Forsyth number once the Board of Assessors sales records arrive.

assessment_ratio.source: Georgia Department of Revenue, Property Tax Valuation (O.C.G.A. § 48-5-7): https://dor.georgia.gov/property-tax-valuation
assessment_ratio.note: Property is assessed at 40% of fair market value unless the law says otherwise.

forsyth_county.source: Forsyth County, 'Forsyth County Commission Adopts Millage Rates' (Aug 8, 2025): county 7.896 (M&O 4.791 + fire 2.805 + bond 0.300) + schools 16.626 (M&O 15.208 + bonds 1.418): https://www.forsythco.com/news/2025/08/forsyth-county-commission-adopts-millage-rates-2025/
forsyth_county.note: Unincorporated Forsyth. These rates were adopted in August 2025 and fund the 2026 budget. On 2026-10-25 no official county page listed newer adopted rates (news reports covered proposed 2026 changes), so this stays until one does. City of Cumming homes pay a city rate on top, which the data can't tell apart.

homestead_exemption.note: Not applied yet, so tax estimates run a little high for a primary residence. Rules differ by county and need an official source.

homeowners_rate_per_1000.unit: dollars per year per $1,000 of home value
homeowners_rate_per_1000.source: Freddie Mac Research, 'The Cost of Homeowners' Insurance' (Mar 20, 2024), 2023 national average for Freddie Mac borrowers: https://www.freddiemac.com/research/insight/homeowners-insurance-costs
homeowners_rate_per_1000.note: National, not Georgia, and premiums have risen since 2023. The home page lets a family type in a real quote instead.

monthly_per_100k.source: My Home by Freddie Mac, 'Breaking down PMI': 'approximately between $30 and $70 per month for every $100,000 borrowed': https://myhome.freddiemac.com/buying/breaking-down-pmi
monthly_per_100k.note: Uses the high end of Freddie Mac's range so the plan doesn't come up short. Real cost depends on credit score and down payment.

required_below_down_payment_percent.source: My Home by Freddie Mac, 'Breaking down PMI': required 'if you make a down payment less than 20%': https://myhome.freddiemac.com/buying/breaking-down-pmi
required_below_down_payment_percent.note: Mortgage insurance is added when the down payment is under this.

percent_of_price.source: CFPB, 'Determine your down payment': 'closing costs (not including your down payment) range from 2-5% of the home purchase price': https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/prepare/determine-your-down-payment/
percent_of_price.note: Uses the high end of the CFPB range so the plan doesn't come up short. The same CFPB page says to subtract closing costs from your cash to get your down payment, which is how the planner does it.

housing_share_of_gross_income.source: CFPB 'Buying a house: monthly payment worksheet': 'A mortgage lending rule of thumb is that your total monthly housing obligations should be no more than 28% of your pre-tax income': https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_buying-a-house_monthly-payment_worksheet.pdf
housing_share_of_gross_income.note: Shown only as a reference line, never as a rule.

comfortable_min_left_percent.unit: percent of take-home pay left after all monthly costs
comfortable_min_left_percent.source: Design choice for this app, explained in 'reason' and on the How the numbers work page (DESIGN.md section 7)
comfortable_min_left_percent.note: At or above this share left = Comfortable.
comfortable_min_left_percent.reason: These cutoffs are this app's own choice, not a lender rule. The label looks at what is left of take-home pay after every monthly bill, including the home (DESIGN.md section 7). Keeping at least 20% left leaves room to save and to absorb a surprise bill; under 10% left means one repair or a short drop in pay could leave the family short. A lender's guideline (housing near 28% of pay before taxes, CFPB) is shown next to it for reference, but it starts from gross pay and ignores the family's other bills, so it isn't used for the label.

stretching_below_left_percent.unit: percent of take-home pay left after all monthly costs
stretching_below_left_percent.source: Design choice for this app, explained in 'reason' and on the How the numbers work page (DESIGN.md section 7)
stretching_below_left_percent.note: Below this share left = Stretching. Between the two = Tight.
stretching_below_left_percent.reason: These cutoffs are this app's own choice, not a lender rule. The label looks at what is left of take-home pay after every monthly bill, including the home (DESIGN.md section 7). Keeping at least 20% left leaves room to save and to absorb a surprise bill; under 10% left means one repair or a short drop in pay could leave the family short. A lender's guideline (housing near 28% of pay before taxes, CFPB) is shown next to it for reference, but it starts from gross pay and ignores the family's other bills, so it isn't used for the label.

max_sales_price.source: Georgia DCA, Georgia Dream page: maximum sales price 'Up to $625,000': https://dca.georgia.gov/affordable-housing/home-ownership/georgia-dream
max_sales_price.note: The page says 'Program information listed here is effective as of July 8, 2026.'

income_limit_1_2_people.source: Georgia DCA, Georgia Dream page, income limit for 1-2 persons: https://dca.georgia.gov/affordable-housing/home-ownership/georgia-dream

income_limit_3_plus_people.source: Georgia DCA, Georgia Dream page, income limit for 3 or more persons: https://dca.georgia.gov/affordable-housing/home-ownership/georgia-dream

rule_of_thumb_low_percent.unit: percent of home value per year
rule_of_thumb_low_percent.source: Fannie Mae, 'How to Build Your Maintenance and Repair Budget': 'The rule of thumb is to budget 1% to 4% of your home’s value per year for maintenance costs, including repairs and replacements.' Newer homes: 1%; homes more than 30 years old: lean toward 4%. https://yourhome.fanniemae.com/own/how-build-your-maintenance-and-repair-budget
rule_of_thumb_low_percent.cite: Fannie Mae rule of thumb, low end (newer homes)
rule_of_thumb_low_percent.note: Shown as a suggestion next to the maintenance box; only what the family types is added to the monthly total.

rule_of_thumb_high_percent.unit: percent of home value per year
rule_of_thumb_high_percent.source: Fannie Mae, 'How to Build Your Maintenance and Repair Budget': 'The rule of thumb is to budget 1% to 4% of your home’s value per year for maintenance costs, including repairs and replacements.' Newer homes: 1%; homes more than 30 years old: lean toward 4%. https://yourhome.fanniemae.com/own/how-build-your-maintenance-and-repair-budget
rule_of_thumb_high_percent.cite: Fannie Mae rule of thumb, high end (homes over 30 years old)
